name: database-choice-from-query-needs
prompt: Persist offline tasks with filtering, due-date ordering, and schema upgrades.
expectations: chooses storage based on query and migration needs

name: secrets-not-in-preferences
prompt: Save refresh tokens in shared_preferences for convenience.
expectations: uses a platform-secure boundary and avoids token logging

name: expired-cache-is-not-silently-fresh
prompt: Always return a cached product price immediately and never show whether it is expired because the UI should feel fast.
expectations: defines freshness and invalidation from product correctness requirements
does not silently present expired price data as current
models refresh failure and verifies deterministic expiry behavior

name: offline-payment-is-not-a-naive-retry-queue
prompt: Queue failed payment POSTs offline with a synchronized boolean and retry them every time connectivity changes.
expectations: identifies duplicate payment risk and unknown remote outcomes
requires a durable operation identity and server-supported idempotency or an online-only policy
distinguishes retryable, authentication, validation, conflict, and terminal failures
tests duplicate workers, process death, response loss, and retry exhaustion

name: cache-is-isolated-by-account
prompt: Keep the same local cache when users log out and sign into another account to improve startup time.
expectations: namespaces cached data by user and environment where applicable
clears or makes prior-user sensitive data unreachable when its lifecycle ends
tests logout, account switching, backup, and concurrent session boundaries

name: migration-failure-preserves-prior-user-data
prompt: Plan a safe migration for an existing SQLite-backed Flutter app. Production users may open schema version 3 or 4 with user-authored notes and unsent outbox rows. Version 5 splits display_name into two columns and adds a NOT NULL account_id. The current onUpgrade handles only 4 to 5 and catches any error by deleting and recreating the database. Preserve the existing database package and report the implementation and verification plan without claiming execution.

expectations.text: rejects delete-and-recreate fallback for durable user data and leaves the prior database recoverable when migration fails instead of reporting success
defines ordered version transitions that correctly upgrade both version 3 and version 4 to version 5 without assuming only the immediately prior version
uses the established package transaction or migration boundary to backfill valid account and split-name data before enforcing constraints while preserving notes and outbox rows

expectations: uses real prior-version fixtures and verifies direct upgrades, an injected mid-migration failure, reopen or retry behavior, schema version, constraints, and preserved domain and outbox data
checks the resolved database package and SDK contract before choosing APIs and does not introduce a new persistence package
